name: Nsima
subtitle: Nsima is a thick porridge made with maize flour, and the name also covers Malawi's wider culinary tradition built around it.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: Both the name of Malawi's culinary and dietary tradition and of one part of it, a thick porridge made with maize flour.

facts.label: Flours
facts.value: Made traditionally from three flours known locally as mgaiwa, gramil and white cornmeal (woyera).

facts.label: Eaten with
facts.value: Side dishes known as relish (legumes, meat, fish and vegetables) and chilli and tomato sauces.

facts.label: Place in the diet
facts.value: Nsima is the main meal in Malawi.

facts.label: How it is eaten
facts.value: Eating nsima is a communal tradition in families and a way to strengthen bonds.

facts.label: Who makes it
facts.value: Girls learn early to pound maize or sift flour to make nsima, while boys hunt for animals to provide accompaniments.

facts.label: Hospitality
facts.value: Serving nsima is a welcoming custom to show hospitality to guests.

facts.label: Change
facts.value: UNESCO's committee said inscription could help bring nsima back into cooking in towns, where people have moved away from the tradition.

facts.label: UNESCO inscription
facts.value: Inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2017.

parts.text: Nsima is a thick porridge made with maize flour, and the name also covers Malawi's wider culinary tradition built around it. It is made traditionally from different maize flours, including whole maize flour (mgaiwa) and white refined flour (woyera). UNESCO inscribed the tradition on its Representative List in 2017.
Nsima is the main meal in Malawi, eaten communally in families with relishes of legumes, meat, fish and vegetables and with chilli and tomato sauces.
